question.problem:
Suppose ${b}_{2}=q{b}_{1}+a$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2}=-4.$ If $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and ${b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, find the value of $q.$ 

*Hint: You might wish to take the equation ${b}_{2}=q{b}_{1}+a$ and find the dot product of both sides with ${b}_{1}.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the equation ${b}_{2}=q{b}_{1}+a$ and find the dot product of both sides with ${b}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} & =q{b}_{1}+a \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}\cdot (q{b}_{1}+a) \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}\cdot (q{b}_{1})+({b}_{1}\cdot a) \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & =q({b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1})+({b}_{1}\cdot a)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the formula for the dot product to compute the values of ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1} & ={b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={3}^{2}+{4}^{2} \\  & =9+16 \\  & =25 \\ {b}_{1}\cdot a & ={b}_{1}{a}_{1}+{b}_{2}{a}_{2} \\  & =3\cdot 1+4\cdot 2 \\  & =3+8 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the values for ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1},$ ${b}_{1}\cdot a,$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & =q({b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1})+({b}_{1}\cdot a) \\ -4 & =q\cdot 25+11 \\ -25q & =15 \\ q & =-\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
